name: Matrix
formal: A matrix $A$ has entries $A_{ij}$, with row $i$ and column $j$. Products satisfy $(AB)_{ij}=\sum_k A_{ik}B_{kj}$.

check.prompt: What does the second index of $A_{ij}$ specify?
check.explanation: The convention is row first, column second.

linkedFormal: A matrix $A$ has entries $A_{ij}$, with row $i$ and column $j$. Products satisfy $(AB)_{ij}=\sum_k A_{ik}B_{kj}$.

name: Matrix Representation
meaning: Numbers describing a state or operator in a chosen basis.
formal: State coordinates are $c_i=\langle i|\psi\rangle$. Operator entries are $A_{ij}=\langle i|A|j\rangle$, so column $j$ contains the coordinates of $A|j\rangle$.

check.prompt: Where do the coefficients of $A|1\rangle$ go?
check.explanation: The input basis index labels the column.

linkedFormal: [[Quantum State|State]] [[Coordinate|coordinates]] are $c_i=\langle i|\psi\rangle$. [[Linear Operator|Operator]] entries are $A_{ij}=\langle i|A|j\rangle$, so column $j$ contains the [[Coordinate|coordinates]] of $A|j\rangle$.

name: Unitary Operator
meaning: An invertible operator that preserves overlaps and lengths.
example: A real rotation matrix is unitary.

check.prompt: For a unitary U, its inverse is…

name: Change of Basis
meaning: Describe the same object using different reference vectors.
formal: If $|e_j\rangle=\sum_i|i\rangle U_{ij}$, with columns the new orthonormal basis in old coordinates, then $c_{new}=U^\dagger c_{old}$ and $A_{new}=U^\dagger A_{old}U$.
example: Taking new basis vectors to be eigenvectors produces a diagonal operator matrix.

check.prompt: When U has new basis vectors as columns, the new matrix is…
check.explanation: Convert new coordinates to old, act, then convert back.

linkedFormal: If $|e_j\rangle=\sum_i|i\rangle U_{ij}$, with columns the new [[Orthonormal Basis|orthonormal basis]] in old [[Coordinate|coordinates]], then $c_{new}=U^\dagger c_{old}$ and $A_{new}=U^\dagger A_{old}U$.

name: Determinant
meaning: A number that detects whether a square matrix can be inverted.
formal: For $A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$, $\det A=ad-bc$. More generally, it is the signed sum over all permutations of column choices. $\det A=0$ exactly when a finite square matrix has a nonzero vector sent to zero.

check.explanation: Multiply the diagonal entries and subtract the other product.

linkedFormal: For $A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$, $\det A=ad-bc$. More generally, it is the signed sum over all permutations of column choices. $\det A=0$ exactly when a finite square [[Matrix|matrix]] has a nonzero [[Vector|vector]] sent to zero.

name: Secular Equation
meaning: The equation whose roots are matrix eigenvalues.

check.explanation: Move the eigenvalue term to the left.

name: Trace
meaning: The sum of a square matrix’s diagonal entries.
formal: $\operatorname{tr}A=\sum_i A_{ii}$. For finite square matrices, $\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA)$, and the trace equals the sum of eigenvalues counted with multiplicity.
linkedFormal: $\operatorname{tr}A=\sum_i A_{ii}$. For finite square matrices, $\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA)$, and the trace equals the sum of [[Eigenvalue|eigenvalues]] counted with [[Multiplicity|multiplicity]].

name: Polynomial
meaning: A finite sum of nonnegative integer powers with numerical coefficients.
formal: $f(x)=\sum_{k=0}^n c_kx^k$, where $n$ is a nonnegative integer and each $c_k$ is a scalar.
linkedFormal: $f(x)=\sum_{k=0}^n c_kx^k$, where $n$ is a nonnegative [[Integer|integer]] and each $c_k$ is a [[Scalar|scalar]].

name: Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
meaning: Every nonconstant polynomial with complex coefficients has a complex root.
formal: If $p(z)$ is a nonconstant complex polynomial, there exists a complex number $\lambda$ with $p(\lambda)=0$. A degree-n polynomial has n roots counted with their repeated occurrences.

check.prompt: Over the complex numbers, a nonconstant polynomial…
check.explanation: This guarantees a finite complex matrix has an eigenvalue.

linkedFormal: If $p(z)$ is a nonconstant complex [[Polynomial|polynomial]], there exists a [[Complex Number Arithmetic|complex number]] $\lambda$ with $p(\lambda)=0$. A degree-n [[Polynomial|polynomial]] has n [[Polynomial Root|roots]] counted with their repeated occurrences.

name: Transpose
meaning: Swap the rows and columns of a matrix.
formal: $(A^T)_{ij}=A_{ji}$. Transposition alone does not complex-conjugate entries.
linkedFormal: $(A^T)_{ij}=A_{ji}$. Transposition alone does not complex-conjugate entries.

name: Inverse Matrix
meaning: A matrix that reverses another matrix’s action.
formal: For a square matrix, $A^{-1}A=AA^{-1}=I$. An inverse exists exactly when the determinant is nonzero.

check.explanation: Composing an action with its inverse returns the input.

linkedFormal: For a square [[Matrix|matrix]], $A^{-1}A=AA^{-1}=I$. An inverse exists exactly when the [[Determinant|determinant]] is nonzero.

name: Diagonal Matrix
meaning: A square matrix whose entries outside the main diagonal are zero.
formal: $D_{ij}=0$ whenever $i\ne j$; its diagonal entries are $D_{ii}$.

check.prompt: Which entries must vanish in a diagonal matrix?
check.explanation: Only the main diagonal can carry nonzero numbers.

linkedFormal: $D_{ij}=0$ whenever $i\ne j$; its diagonal entries are $D_{ii}$.

name: Polynomial Root
meaning: An input making a polynomial’s output zero.

check.explanation: Substituting the root makes the output zero.

name: Null Space
meaning: All vectors that a linear map sends to zero.
formal: $\ker A=\{v:Av=0\}$. A square finite matrix is singular when its null space contains a nonzero vector.

check.prompt: A vector in the null space satisfies…
check.explanation: The matrix can be nonzero while annihilating some vectors.

linkedFormal: $\ker A=\{v:Av=0\}$. A square finite [[Matrix|matrix]] is singular when its null space contains a nonzero [[Vector|vector]].
